title: Why an Engagement Ring 'Should' Cost 3 Months' Pay
alts: The Diamond Company That Invented Your Ring Budget
Why Your Diamond Loses Half Its Value the Second You Buy It
line1: A jeweler told Dave a ring should cost three months' salary. That rule isn't tradition -- a diamond company invented it to sell more diamonds.
summary: Dave is ring shopping, and the salesman says the ring should cost three months' salary. We trace that 'rule' back to De Beers' famous 1947 'A Diamond Is Forever' campaign, and how the suggested number quietly climbed from one month to two, then three in Japan. Then the money: the 50-200% retail markup on diamonds, why a ring can lose half its value the moment you leave the store, and the lab-grown diamond price crash that's cut prices 75-90% versus mined stones. Plus what couples are really spending in 2025 (The Knot's Real Weddings Study), who actually profits from the old rule, and practical, romance-friendly ways to buy a ring on your own terms. Education, not advice.
